description: Toy Box Friends G2-15 (grade 2): find the rule of a growing or shrinking number pattern (add or take away the same number), check every jump on the shelf and on a number line, continue it, fill a gap and fix a broken pattern.

youtube.title: Number Pattern Machine! Find the Rule | Grade 2 Math | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
The Pattern Machine in the lab is jammed: 2, 5, 8, 11... what comes next? Robo guesses 12, but the machine only accepts the right number! Cat shows how to find the rule: check the jump from every number to the next (add 3, add 3, add 3), then see the same equal jumps on a number line. We catch Robo changing the rule halfway, count down with take away 2 and take away 5, fill missing numbers, spot odd and even patterns, make our own pattern with Mouse, and fix the Broken Machine.

For second graders (CCSS 2.NBT.B.8, 2.OA.C.3: number patterns, add and take away, odd and even).

Try at home: build block towers 2, 4 and 6 blocks tall and predict the next one. Then pick a start number and a rule, say four numbers, and let a grown-up find your rule. Keep small blocks away from babies.

do.text: Robo, you guessed before you checked. Let's find the machine's rule first.
A number pattern follows a rule. The rule tells us the jump.
From 2 to 5. How much is the jump?
2, then 3, 4, 5. That's a jump of 3. Add 3.
Not yet! We check every jump, not just the first one.
Another way: count on. From 5, say 6, 7, 8. That's three steps.
Every jump is the same. Add 3, every step!
Now watch the same pattern on a number line.
Every leap is the same length. Same rule, same jump!
Where will the ball land next?
My turn! I made a pattern. 3, 6, 9, 13.
Let's check every jump. 3 to 6, add 3. 6 to 9, add 3.
Oops. I changed the rule halfway.
A pattern keeps the same rule at every step. So what should come after 9?
That's why we check every jump, not just the first one.
What's the jump? Each number is smaller.
Let's step back on the number line. Next comes 12, then 10.
Take away 2 each time. 29 take away 2 is 27!
Take away 5 each time. Next is 80!
Jump forward three hops for add 3. Step back two for take away 2!
Find the rule first. 4 to 8 is add 4. 16 to 20 is add 4.
8 add 4 is 12. And 12 add 4 is 16. It checks out!
Add 5. 20 add 5 is 25, and 25 add 5 is 30.
Add 10 each time. The tens digit grows by one, and the ones digit stays 7.
Fun fact! A calendar hides a pattern. Go down one row, and you add 7.
Check every step, and you'll know the plan!
Two patterns with the same rule, add 2. One starts at 1.
1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Add 2 from an odd number, and every number is odd.
2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Start even, and every number is even.
Even numbers make pairs. Odd numbers have one left over.
Fun fact! On many streets, one side has odd house numbers. The other side is even.
Mouse, our lab helper, will load a start number and a rule.
6, 11, 16, 21. Look at the ones digits: 6, 1, 6, 1. They take turns!
Make your own! Pick a start, like 3, and a rule, like add 10.
3, 13, 23, 33. The tens digit grows by one each time!
Challenge mode! Find the next number.
Take away 3 every time. 21 take away 3 is 18!
22 to 27 is add 5. So 12 add 5 is 17. And 17 add 5 is 22!
Warning! Broken pattern. One number is wrong.
Which number is broken? Check every jump.
Add 3, add 3, then add 2, then add 4. The jumps change at 14!
With add 3, 12 add 3 is 15. Swap in 15!
Is 2, 4, 7, 9 a pattern with one rule?
No. The jumps are add 2, add 3, add 2. They change.
Start at 1 and add 2: 1, 3, 5, 7. Odd or even?
Let's remember. Find the jump. Check every step. Then continue the pattern, or fill the gap.
A rule can add or take away. Checked every step!
Try it at home! Build block towers 2, 4 and 6 tall. How tall is the next one?
Keep small blocks away from babies
